evidence: src/application/services/CancelBookingService.ts, method cancel(): `if (booking === undefined) throw new HttpError(404, `No booking ${bookingId}`);` — choosing an HTTP 404 status is transport/presentation responsibility inside an application-layer use case.
The rest of cancel() (bookings.findById, booking.cancel(), payments.refund, bookings.save, notifications.send, toBookingView) is proper application orchestration through ports.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Most of CancelBookingService does normal application-layer work. It loads the booking through a repository port, calls the domain method booking.cancel(), issues a refund and sends a notification through outbound ports, and maps the result to a view DTO. One responsibility is in the wrong layer: when the booking is missing, cancel() throws HttpError(404, ...). Picking an HTTP status code is a transport (presentation) concern, so the use case is coupled to HTTP. The application layer should signal a protocol-neutral failure, such as a BookingNotFound error or a result value, and the inbound HTTP adapter should turn that into a 404. The import of HttpError from adapters/inbound is an import-direction issue and is out of scope here. This judgment rests on the HTTP status-mapping responsibility itself.
